casey:go-vegetarian:
Your current lifestyle puts your annual carbon footprint at 10,510 kg CO2e, and going fully vegetarian — while keeping your dairy habits exactly as they are now — would cut that by 2,605 kg CO2e per year, a 25% reduction on its own. That single dietary shift is the equivalent of planting 43 trees and letting them grow for ten years, which shows just how much your five red meat meals a week are driving your emissions.

Start by swapping one red meat meal at a time with a plant-based alternative you already enjoy — legumes, eggs, tofu, or cheese-based dishes all count since you're keeping dairy. By the end of your first month, aim to have replaced all five weekly red meat meals with vegetarian options so the change becomes routine rather than an effort. Stock your kitchen ahead of time so that on busy nights, a vegetarian meal is actually the easier choice, not the harder one. Once going vegetarian feels natural, you can look at other areas — like setting your thermostat back overnight — to build on that 25% saving and reduce your 10,510 kg footprint further.
casey:next-car-ev:
Your current footprint sits at 10,510 kg CO2e per year, and switching your gas car to an electric vehicle is the single most impactful move you can make right now. Because you're already driving 320 km a week, you don't need to change your habits at all — the savings come purely from switching the technology under you. Making that swap would cut 2,516 kg CO2e from your annual footprint, which is 24% of your total — the equivalent of 42 trees growing for ten years.

Start by researching EV models that fit your weekly driving pattern, since 320 km a week is well within the range of most current electric vehicles. Look into Ontario's available federal rebates and incentives, which can meaningfully reduce the upfront purchase cost and make the switch more financially realistic. When your current vehicle is due for replacement — or sooner if it makes financial sense — commit to making your next car electric rather than returning to a gas model. In the meantime, call your insurance provider and your employer to understand any EV-related perks or charging support you may already have access to.
casey:swap-beef-plant:
Here is your action plan.

Your current carbon footprint is 10,510 kg CO2e per year, and a single dietary shift can make a meaningful dent in that number. You currently eat 5 red meat meals a week, so swapping just 2 of those for beans, lentils, or tofu would save an estimated 998 kg CO2e per year — that is 9% of your total footprint. To make this concrete, pick two specific days now, such as Monday and Wednesday, and commit to those as your plant-based meal days before the week begins. Stock your kitchen with a few staples — canned lentils, dried beans, or firm tofu — so the swap requires no extra shopping trip in the moment. Over a full year, those two swapped meals a week add up to the equivalent of 17 trees growing for ten years, without changing your driving, your flights, or your home heating at all. Start this week with one meal, get comfortable with it, and add the second within the first month.
sam:one-fewer-long-haul:
Your current footprint is 5,631 kg CO2e per year, and because you don't drive and eat vegetarian, your six long-haul return flights are doing the heavy lifting — they're a dominant part of what's left to address. Dropping just one of those trips would save 759 kg CO2e per year, which is 13% of your total footprint, equivalent to 13 trees growing for ten years.

Start by looking at your flight calendar and identifying the one trip that could most realistically be replaced or skipped — a conference that could be attended virtually, a visit that could shift to every other year, or a destination reachable by a longer but lower-impact route. Since your diet is already vegetarian with medium dairy, this single flight change is genuinely the highest-leverage move available to you right now. Once you've identified the candidate trip, make a concrete decision before next year's bookings open so the choice doesn't drift. That one decision — five fewer flights instead of six — delivers more carbon reduction than most people achieve with years of smaller habit changes.
